A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SewingLDM study. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and supplementary material support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original garment-generation and simulation results, quantitative comparisons, a 30-participant user study, and ablations in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds reconstruction measurements, concurrent-method comparisons, a representation ablation, and additional sketch-conditioned generation examples.

M1.justification: The 29-dimensional edge representation, quantized autoencoder, DiT diffusion model, two-stage training and attention-output fine-tuning remain unchanged. Equations (1)-(4) are retained. The added panel-order listing documents implementation without establishing a procedural revision.

E1.justification: The 120,000-pattern GarmentCodeData corpus and garment-generation task remain. V2 expands input-scenario coverage with explicitly sourced Multimodal Garment Designer images and hand-drawn sketches (Figures 6, 17 and 18), providing a focused extension of the existing sketch-conditioned evaluation.

E2.justification: V2 adds direct qualitative comparisons with ChatGarment and AIpparel in supplementary Section 8 and Figure 11, substantially updating the evaluated competition. Existing comparators, including GarmentCode, remain. Design2GarmentCode is discussed but is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: V2 adds test-set reconstruction and simulation-failure evaluation, fine-tunes SewFormer until validation loss plateaus, and evaluates DressCode failure rate using its existing checkpoint. Section 4.2 also changes the main sewing-pattern comparison inputs from ControlNet-generated images to selected in-the-wild images. These reported protocol changes do not establish that retained Table 1 experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds an illustrative extended-versus-original representation comparison testing neckline and skirt-detail preservation (Section 10, Figure 12), plus additional sketch-generalization examples. The compression, attention, injection-depth and one-stage-versus-two-stage ablations, use case and failure examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed evaluations, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The user-study reporting practice remains unchanged; newly reported failure percentages are outcome metrics, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports Panel L2 values of 0.64 for the autoencoder, 3.13 for SewingLDM and 12.3 for fine-tuned SewFormer, alongside other reconstruction metrics. Section 4.3 adds DressCode's 11.4% failure rate. Section 8 reports comparable results to ChatGarment and better results than AIpparel. Table 1 and the renumbered compression table retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(5), the representation definitions, quantization rule and codebook-usage calculation remain unchanged. V2 adds implementation explanations and standard evaluation-metric descriptions, without new proofs, formal derivations or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract and three central contributions remain substantively stable. The introduction strengthens the compression claim by asserting fixed memory consumption and scalability to more intricate designs, and explicitly emphasizes fitting bodies without detailed body measurements.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving token-budget and GPU constraints, clarifies conditioning as a normalized residual, and connects baseline fitting failures to body-training and attachment limitations. The stated limitations concerning pockets, zippers and intricate sketches remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Supplementary Sections 6 and 9 newly document the canonical panel ordering, parameter-to-description thresholds, GPT-4 annotation refinement and its prompt, and PiDiNet checkpoint usage. These substantially expand reproducibility information. Hardware, training times and loss weights remain unchanged; the explicit future code-release promise is removed while the project link remains.

R1.justification: V2 acknowledges that concurrent methods already support complex garment features and adds substantive positioning against ChatGarment, AIpparel and Design2GarmentCode. Section 8 distinguishes category-specific parameterization and body adaptation, updating the earlier positioning centered on DressCode, SewFormer and GarmentCode.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized language corrections and rewrites parts of the introduction and experimental discussion. It expands the supplementary organization and moves the use case from main Section 4.5 to supplementary Section 13. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain.

P2.justification: V2 adds reconstruction and annotation-prompt tables and figures for concurrent comparisons, representation analysis and additional sketch conditions. Main Figure 6 is replaced, while much of its earlier comparison reappears in supplementary Figure 16 with revised input illustrations. The use-case figure moves to the supplement; existing ablation and body-shape galleries are retained.

improvement.justification: V1's compression validation relied heavily on qualitative examples and binary reconstruction checks. V2's direct reconstruction and simulation-failure measurements substantially strengthen evidence for a central contribution. Concurrent-method comparisons and explicit panel-order and annotation instructions also improve assessment and reproducibility. Generalization evidence remains illustrative and statistical uncertainty remains unreported, but the additions address important evidential gaps while retaining the established results.
